Can't find what you're looking for? Contact Us What is an autonomous mobile robot (AMR)? Collapse An Autonomous Mobile Robot (AMR) is an industrial vehicle that uses onboard artificial intelligence, sensors, and mapping technology to navigate facilities independently. Unlike traditional systems or manual forklifts, AMRs understand their environment in real time. They safely transport materials, pallets, and carts around dynamic facilities without requiring human operators or infrastructure modifications. Seegrid's fleet of AMRs automates up to 80% of non-conveyed material moves across manufacturing, warehousing and logistics facilities. What is the difference between an AGVs and AMRs? Expand The primary difference is how they navigate: Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) follow fixed infrastructure like magnetic tape, floor wires, or QR codes. If an obstacle blocks an AGV’s path, it stops and waits until the obstruction is cleared. Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) use 3D laser mapping and AI to understand their surroundings and can adapt to changing facility layouts without physical reconfiguration. Seegrid combines the best of both worlds through Sliding Scale Autonomy . Our vehicles deliver AGV-like predictability on highly repetitive long-haul routes while utilizing AMR-like agility for complex tasks like pallet manipulation and dynamic path planning. How do Seegrid AMRs navigate without floor tape or wires? Expand Seegrid AMRs navigate using proprietary GRID Engine software fused with 3D LiDAR SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping). When first deployed, the robot is walked through the facility to build a highly detailed 3D digital map of the space. During daily operation, onboard perception sensors constantly match the robot's real-time view against this map, as well as continually recreate the map to eliminate map aging. This allows the vehicle to reliably pick and drop pallets—even yawed or misaligned ones—with precision in crowded, dynamic environments. What industries and applications use Seegrid autonomous vehicles? Expand Seegrid AMRs are built for high-throughput environments in three primary sectors: Manufacturing: Used for parts-to-line delivery, material transport, and removing finished goods from production lines. Warehousing: Ideal for high-density racking, vertical pallet placement (up to 15 feet high), and autonomous buffer management. Logistics & 3PL: Deployed for cross-docking, long-haul cart tugging, and trash removal. Our solutions are engineered to help facilities reduce labor dependencies, eliminate forklift-related injuries, and lower inventory requirements by up to 30%. Can humans safely work alongside Seegrid AMRs? Expand Seegrid AMRs are the market leader in robust navigation, and go above and beyond ANSI B56.5 safety standards , as well as satisfy all applicable safety requirements of ANSI R15.08. Our robots work seamlessly–and safely–alongside their human coworkers. Autonomy that works with you.
